_about: Key places on the map: 3 to 5 per region, only places an official source names, each line backed by its cite (owner card 18 Oct 2026, style B name chips). Shown while one of the listed places is selected. Positions are OpenStreetMap points (data/SOURCES.md, Map flags).

flags.name: Haro
flags.line: Rioja's westernmost town. A French firm in its station quarter hired a champagne maker from Reims in 1890.

flags.name: Sierra de Cantabria
flags.line: The mountains on the northern side. They shelter Rioja Alta, and Rioja Alavesa even more.

flags.name: Ebro
flags.line: The vineyards lie on both banks of the river. Alluvial soils near the rivers make up half the land.

flags.name: Alfaro
flags.line: Rioja's easternmost town, 100 km down the valley from Haro.

flags.name: Jerez de la Frontera
flags.line: One of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.

flags.name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda
flags.line: One of the three ageing towns. Manzanilla has its own DO named after it.

flags.name: El Puerto de Santa María
flags.line: The third of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.

flags.name: Guadalete
flags.line: The river is the southern edge of the area where Sherry is aged.

flags.name: Chipiona
flags.line: Moscatel may also be aged here, and in Chiclana.
